newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian woman dies of anthrax.
newsitem.headline: Russian woman dies of anthrax.

text.p: A 31-year-old Russian woman died from anthrax after meat from animals suspected of having the disease was handed out to farm workers as part of their wages, Itar-Tass news agency said on Sunday.
It said 23 more people were taken to hospital and 1,500 were put under medical observation after the woman died in the village of Troitskoye, 300 km (190 miles) south-east of Moscow.
The tragic incident reflected the lack of sanitary controls at many Russian farms and food plants.

Tass said that suspicions were raised in the village when nine cows and a horse died mysteriously. Samples from the dead animals, along with meat from three sick young cows which had been slaughtered, were sent to a laboratory.
Scientists reported that the animals had anthrax, but by then the meat had been handed out to farm workers and had also been delivered to five schools.
Anthrax cases were almost unheard of for many years in Russia but Tass said the woman was the fifth person to have died of the disease in the last two years alone.
Anthrax is usually carried by sheep and cows. It can be contracted by human beings and those affected can develop festering boils and die in agony.
